Cards & decisions

01 — BY WORRY

Start from a decision

Open a theme close to yours to read what the decision is really about, how to sort it out, and the cards connected to it.

WORKWork & Career

  • Changing jobsIn your current job, is there an improvement you haven't tried yet?
  • Job huntingIf you didn't have to care what people around you think, what kind of company would you want to choose?
  • A side jobHow many hours a week do you have available for a side job?
  • Going independentEven if months with zero income continued, how many months could you withstand?
  • Learning something newWhen you've finished this learning, what state do you want to be in?
  • Leaving a jobIf you had to name just one reason you want to quit, what would it be?
  • Taking time offFever, sleep, appetite, concentration — roughly how many points would you give each?
  • A job offerIs the condition you're catching on something that would move if you negotiated, or something that touches the company's essence?
  • A transferWhat meaning do the role and the length of the posting hold for your career?
  • A qualificationHaving gained the qualification, what do you want to change?
  • Studying abroadWhat do you truly want to gain from studying abroad — language ability, a degree, or the experience itself?
  • Going back to schoolIs what you want to learn knowledge directly tied to your work, or an education that widens your own world?
  • Telling work about a side jobWhat do your company's work rules actually stipulate about side jobs?

LOVELove & Family

  • LoveWhen you're with the other person, can you be yourself?
  • MarriageWhat do you want to gain by marrying, and what are you afraid of losing?
  • Breaking upWithin this relationship, how much of the time can you be yourself?
  • CaregivingCould you continue the current form of caregiving a year from now?
  • Confessing feelingsHow long have these feelings continued?
  • A giftWhat has the other person been having trouble with lately, or seemed to want?
  • A weddingWhose is this ceremony, and what is it for?
  • Getting back togetherIs what you want to return to the person themselves, or the sense of security of those days?

LIFEDaily Life, Money & People

  • Moving houseWhat stresses you most about your current home, and would moving really resolve it?
  • Money & buyingHow would having it change your everyday life?
  • RelationshipsAfter meeting that person, how do you feel?
  • Buying a carIf you had this car, how would your weekly life change in concrete terms?
  • Sleepless nightsIs what is going around in your head right now fact, or imagination?
  • Go or notIf you had to name one reason you want to go, what would it be?
  • Saying noIs the reason you want to say no the content, the volume, or the timing?
  • Reaching outIn one sentence, what is the purpose of this message?
  • ApologizingOf what happened to the other person, what weighed heaviest?
  • Canceling a contractIn the last three months, how many times did you actually use it?
  • TravelWhat do you most want from this trip — rest, a break from the everyday, or time with someone?
  • InvestingHow much, out of surplus funds that won't affect your life, can you put into investing?
  • InsuranceWhat do you fear most — in which situation, and a shortfall of how much?
  • Lending moneyIs the amount requested within a range that wouldn't affect your life even if it didn't come back?
  • Drinks with colleaguesIn your condition today, could you enjoy it through to the end?
  • A petWhere in your current life would you place the time for daily care?

OTHEROther decisions

  • Buying a homeCould you continue the monthly repayments even if your income fell by twenty percent?
  • Own or rentWhen you compare under the same conditions, how large is the difference in the total over ten years?
  • Leaving the family homeCan you state the upfront costs of living alone and your monthly living expenses in numbers?

04 — FAQ

Frequently asked questions

How many tarot cards are there in total?

There are 78. They consist of the 22 Major Arcana, which represent life's larger flow and themes, and the 56 Minor Arcana (four suits — Wands, Cups, Swords, and Pentacles — of 14 cards each), which represent everyday events and feelings. On this page, all 78 cards are explained one by one.

How does the meaning change between upright and reversed?

Upright means the card's theme is coming to the surface; reversed means the theme is excessive, lacking, or turned inward. A reversed card does not mean something “bad” — it is a sign to change how you approach it. Each card's page explains both.

Does the reading change depending on the decision I'm facing, even for the same card?

Yes, it does. For example, The Tower can be read as the collapse of an assumption when you're thinking about changing jobs, and as a chance to reconsider a relationship when you're thinking about love. Each card's page includes a section, “Reading it for your decision,” with interpretations for different situations.

Do I need to memorize the tarot meanings to use them?

No memorization is needed. The cards are not a tool to predict your future, but questions to help you organize your own thinking. Just reading the keywords of the card you drew and the “questions to ask yourself” can help you notice feelings and conditions you had overlooked.

Which card should I start reading from?

We recommend starting from the theme closest to what you're torn about right now. The guide by decision brings together, for each of 40 themes such as changing jobs, love, money, and moving house, the cards involved and viewpoints for organizing your thoughts. If you have already drawn a card, please start from that card's page.
